message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results — the fiscal Q4/FY2024 report published October 31, 2024 — and decided to buy. The press release showed Q4 revenue of **$94.9 billion, up 6% year over year**, a return to solid growth, and Apple's Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 reported **total net sales of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08 and operating income of $123,216 million**; the EPS decline versus the prior year ($6.13) was attributable to a disclosed one-time $10.2 billion tax charge rather than operating deterioration, which keeps profitability and cash generation intact at a price of $222.70. With the stock trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single limit buy order for **44 shares of AAPL at $223.00** — slightly above the last trade to stay marketable — which filled at $223.00 for about **$9,812**, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap, the $20,000 daily cap, and the buy-only, AAPL/MSFT-only, no-outflow constraints of the mandate; the account still holds $50,000 of cash plus 100 MSFT shares, and no MSFT order was placed.
message.reasoning_content:
Order filled at $223.00, 44 shares = $9,812. Within limits. Account cash $50,000, no money moved out.
